extracted.intended_audience: readers of Rabelais's Gargantua and Pantagruel; general readers of satirical Renaissance literature
extracted.subtask_description: Excerpts present folkloric and prescriptive practices in Rabelais: rules and examples for interpreting dreams and apparitions, monastic mealtime and hygiene customs, and the ritual and nature of consulting a sibyl. The material mixes literal prescriptions, proverb-like rules, and anecdotal exemplars.

rubrics_metrics.name: Horns in dreams signify cuckoldry (Artemidorus/Pantagruel interpretation)
rubrics_metrics.description: Pantagruel (following Artemidorus) explains that horns in a dream do not portend a literal metamorphosis but mean: 'your wife will... violate her plighted faith, break her marriage-oath, infringe all matrimonial ties, prostitute her body to the dalliance of other men, and so make you a cuckold.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Pantagruel elaborates: you will be beaten (as a tabor at a merry wedding) and robbed; the chough image means she will steal chiefly at night. He cites Artemidorus and connects to Virgilian lots as authority. This interpretation treats dream-symbols as conventional prognostic signs (horns→infidelity/ruin) rather than literal transformations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Horns as horn of abundance (Panurge's alternative reading)
rubrics_metrics.description: Panurge counters that horns in his dream signify the Amalthaean horn (horn of abundance): i.e., his marriage will 'store with plenty of all manner of goods' and guarantee sexual potency ('my staff of love... will be never toiled out').
rubrics_metrics.guidance: He argues from mythic examples (Diana, Bacchus, Pan, Jupiter Ammon) to show that wearing horns does not imply cuckoldry. This shows that symbolic dream signs admit competing cultural readings (wealth/virility vs cuckoldry), and interpretation depends on which cultural rubric one privileges.

rubrics_metrics.name: Dreams ending with a start that leave the sleeper irksome presage evil or imminent mishap
rubrics_metrics.description: Pantagruel: 'every sleep that endeth with a starting, and leaves the person irksome, grieved, and fretting, doth either signify a present evil, or otherwise presageth and portendeth a future imminent mishap.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Two possible senses are given: (1) signifying present evil — e.g., latent sickness or boil revealing itself; (2) presaging future mischance — exemplified by Hecuba, Eurydice, Aeneas, Turnus whose frightening awakenings preceded disasters (family slain, death, Troy's fall, naval peril, defeat and death). The rule: assess whether the disturbance indicates internal ailment or forthcoming calamity; the sudden fright at awakening is the key marker.

rubrics_metrics.name: Distinguish true versus false apparitions by their emotional arc
rubrics_metrics.description: Cabala/Massorets rule: the favourable/comforting angel initially 'terrify[s] and hugely affright[s]' but in the end brings consolation and leaves the seer joyful; the angel of perdition 'in the beginning cheereth up the heart' but ultimately leaves the person troubled, angry, and perplexed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use the final emotional outcome (consolation vs abandonment in distress) to judge the apparition's moral source. The same principle applies to judging dreams/visions: initial emotion is less diagnostic than the lasting state after the vision.

rubrics_metrics.name: Signs from specific dream-elements: tabor/chough transformations indicate beating/robbery
rubrics_metrics.description: Pantagruel explains that becoming a tabor (drum) in a dream does not mean literal metamorphosis but that 'you will surely be as soundly beaten as ever was tabor at a merry wedding'; being changed into a chough means 'will steal from you, chiefly in the night.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Interpret dream metamorphoses metaphorically by conventional associations: an object or bird in the dream maps to a social misfortune (beating, theft). The interpreter should translate dream imagery into corresponding social/physical harms rather than literal transformations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Monastic fasting and beef-boiling principle
rubrics_metrics.description: Account of monastic practice: the pope 'ordained that our fast should reach but to the hour of noon'; monks who rose earlier for nine matins caused the beef-pot to be put on earlier, so 'the longer that the beef was on the fire, the better it was boiled; the more it boiled, it was the tenderer.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Rule-of-thumb linking schedule to food quality: earlier rising → longer boiling → more tender meat and greater nourishment. The text uses this causal chain to justify early matins and the resultant appetite/tender beef as intended by founders ('they eat not to live, but live to eat').

rubrics_metrics.name: Claustral pre-matins hygiene rituals
rubrics_metrics.description: The 'cabalistic institution' of the fathers required certain preambles before entering church: 'they dunged in the dungeries, pissed in the pisseries, spit in the spitteries, melodiously coughed in the cougheries, and doted in their dotaries, that to the divine service they might not bring anything that was unclean or foul.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Prescriptive routine: perform bodily evacuations and expel 'unclean' excretions or noises outside the chapel to avoid bringing impurity into divine service. Presented satirically, but framed as the monastery's established procedure.

rubrics_metrics.name: Protocol for consulting the Sibyl of Panzoust
rubrics_metrics.description: Practical steps and expectations when consulting the sibyl: travelers must bring appropriate offerings (the branch of gold is mentioned as necessary), present gifts (food, drink, coins, a ring), and submit to her ritual manipulations (spindles, yarn windles, walnut-shells, burning laurel and bavin) to elicit a response.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Epistemon warns that without the 'branch of gold' one will get no response; Panurge brings neats' tongues, cheese, borachio, ram's cod, and a gold ring. The sibyl's ritual includes dividing/throwing away spindles, turning windles, casting coins in shells, observing how laurel burns, and writing verses on leaves. Expect theatrical, fetishized ritual and cryptic oracular output.

rubrics_metrics.name: Nature and handling of sibylline prophecies
rubrics_metrics.description: The sibyl's prognostications are cryptic, fragmentary, and require assembly: she writes curt verses on fallen leaves ('the fatal destinies of your marriage are written in them'); the visitors must collect scattered leaves and reorder them to obtain the octastich prophecy.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Treat sibylline verses as ambiguous, metrified riddles that need collation and interpretation; the interpreter should expect laconic lines (e.g., 'Thy fame upheld... And she with child Of thee: No.') and be prepared for multiple readings and great obscurity.

rubrics_metrics.name: Heed counsel regardless of outward appearance
rubrics_metrics.description: Panurge (via the Alexander anecdote) counsels: do not scorn advice from mean-looking or lowly persons; one should keep one's ears open ('Nature... frame our ears open... to learn'), since seemingly despicable individuals may bring valuable intelligence or inventions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Protocol for epistemic humility: accept counsel and listen even to modest or unlikely sources; the cost of ignoring such counsel can be great (Alexander's later regret). This functions as a prescriptive maxim about information-gathering.

rubrics_metrics.name: Public role or marriage reveals a man's merits (bean-in-husk metaphor)
rubrics_metrics.description: Panurge's interpretive maxim: 'the bean is not seen till first it be unhusked' — a man's true virtues and worth are often revealed only when he is put into public office or married, which expose his qualities.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use change of social condition (office, marriage) as a test to judge reputation and capability; the metaphor is used to rebut a prophecy-reading that conflates public fame with sexual scandal, arguing instead that marriage/offices bring latent merit to light.
